look_here_first: MUCRONATE SPRANGLETOP (subsp. mucronata) — annual with many slender ascending branches along a central axis and 2–4(-5)-flowered tiny spikelets. Short truncate/irregular membranous true ligule and raised-base sheath hairs must be inspected on the target itself. Four Central Texas Bob Harms comparison images show DIFFERENT subspecies brachiata, not a confirmed mucronata; the two separately labelled native green sprangletop photographs show larger multi-flowered units. Do not equate species complex or background other subspecies with target.

best_field_traits: ANNUAL: tufted or several shoots from an annual fibrous-rooted base; not the longer-lived robust perennial green sprangletop.
PANICLE: many rather straight ascending narrow branches along an elongated central axis, often narrow or somewhat brush-like, and with tiny spikelets attached along sides.
SPIKELET: very small, commonly ~2–4 mm long; about 2–4 florets. Under a lens count florets INSIDE one spikelet rather than spikelets along a branch.
GLUMES: narrow bracts subtending each spikelet; the minute MUCRONATE upper tip is a tiny pointed projection, not necessarily a visible long awn. Exact subspecies anatomy remains unphotographed.
LEAF SHEATH: some distinctly spreading hairs can arise from small raised/bulbous or papillose bases; inspect actual sheath with 10–20× rather than assuming in the whole-plant photo.
LIGULE: membranous with fringed/jagged upper margin; measure actual specimen, do not infer from hairs outside the sheath.
TAXONOMY CAUTION: subsp. mucronata is accepted by POWO; historical Leptochloa mucronata is a synonym. Other subspecies in the D. panicea complex may look similar and need voucher-level checks.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Connected WHOLE ANNUAL: rooted fibrous plant, full brush-like panicle and ruler; document lack of perennial rootstock.
PANICLE BRANCH INSERTION: central axis showing many thin, mostly ascending branches with attached spikelets; overall habit alone is provisional.
SPIKELET MACRO 10–20×: mature 2–4 mm spikelet with a millimeter scale, floret count and glumes clearly separated.
UPPER GLUME MACRO 20×: show any actual minute mucro (tiny hard point) and distinguish it from an awn, with photographed glume tip and scale.
LEAF SHEATH AND LIGULE 10–20×: papillose/bulbous hair bases and true membranous leaf-collar ligule; no arrow until photo visibly resolves the structure.
SUBSPECIES CHECK: authenticated herbarium macro for mucronata versus brachiata at same scale; preserve unresolved determination if only a species-level photograph exists.
MATCHED LOOK-ALIKE: side-by-side measured 2–4-flowered Dinebra spikelet and 4–13-flowered Disakisperma spikelet, each with full rooted plant.
crew_field_check: MUCRONATE SPRANGLETOP — think FINE-BRANCHED ANNUAL: an often slender warm-season annual with NUMEROUS almost straight ascending flowering branches scattered along a main axis, like a narrow brush. Check a mature tiny spikelet with 10–20×: typically 2–4 florets in a ca. 2–4 mm laterally flattened spikelet; short glumes and a tiny pointed glume tip (mucro) require a lens, and do NOT by themselves prove subspecies. Look at the leaf sheath for distinct bulbous/papillose-based spreading hairs and examine the true membranous ligule. The existing source photograph shows only broad panicle/leaf features: it cannot certify floret number, sheath-hair bases, glume mucro or mucronata versus other D. panicea subspecies.

GREEN SPRANGLETOP / Disakisperma dubium: generally a larger perennial arising from a lasting base, commonly with fewer longer near-fingerlike branches, and larger 4–12 mm spikelets containing about 4–13 florets. MUCRONATE SPRANGLETOP / Dinebra panicea subsp. mucronata: slender ANNUAL with many ascending slender branches, generally much smaller ~2–4 mm spikelets with ~2–4 florets and often bulbous-based sheath hairs. Counts can overlap at 4 florets, so a single spikelet count isn't decisive. ERAGROSTIS lovegrasses: many have an airy panicle too but individual spikelets have several fertile florets in overlapping ranks, and the branching/spikelet anatomy differs. Within DINEBRA, the other subspecies of D. panicea can look extremely similar; a photograph labeled merely Dinebra panicea is NOT independently sufficient to certify subsp. mucronata. Old Leptochloa mucronata refers to this taxon in the Kew treatment; Leptochloa filiformis and other older names have been applied differently in historical treatments.

If the plant is only photographed as a whole brush-like head, label at most Dinebra panicea complex / sprangletop candidate pending attached glumes and floret measurements. Preserve subspecies record without inventing certainty.

reconciliation_20261022.measured_check: Existing canonical lesson describes roughly 2–4 mm spikelets with 2–4 florets, a minute glume mucro, papillose-based sheath hairs and a membranous ligule. These must be measured on a verified specimen; the single existing photo cannot prove them.
reconciliation_20261022.lookalikes: Disakisperma dubium is generally perennial with larger, more-flowered spikelets; other Dinebra panicea subspecies require direct infraspecific comparison. Do not identify subspecies from a species-level photograph.
reconciliation_20261022.photo_gap: Rooted annual, branch insertion, mature spikelets and upper glume tip at 10–20× with mm ruler, sheath hair bases and true ligule, authenticated subspecies comparison. No new arrows without visible structure.
reconciliation_20261022.taxonomy_hold: Subspecies identity remains unverified from available photographs; preserve original canonical taxonomic status.
reconciliation_20261022.public_ready: Do not declare fully finished or subspecies photo-verified until specimen determination, public-rights and arrow QA are complete.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · IS IT AN ANNUAL?
field_id_short_tiles.short: Slender, fibrous-rooted grass; no lasting perennial crown
field_id_short_tiles.details: Trace an attached plant downward. Mucronate sprangletop is an annual and can have culms bending at lower nodes. Native green sprangletop (Disakisperma dubium) normally has a robust persistent perennial base. A disconnected flowering branch doesn't prove lifespan.
field_id_short_tiles.photo_status: ATTACHED TARGET ROOT/WHOLE PLANT NOT VERIFIED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · FOLLOW THE FINGERS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Many fine side racemes distributed along a long central axis
field_id_short_tiles.details: The flower head can look like a narrow brush with numerous slender, nearly straight branches inserted at separate positions. The newly archived Bob Harms photographs are of the different subsp. brachiata; use them to learn shared architecture, NOT to confirm subsp. mucronata.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · OPEN THE LEAF
field_id_short_tiles.short: Check short membranous ligule AND raised-base sheath hairs
field_id_short_tiles.details: NEW direct photo 190322lg by Jim Conrad from source-labelled ssp. mucronata visibly separates the whitish ragged membranous ligule at leaf blade/sheath junction from long white sheath hairs BELOW; both have explicit accurate broad arrows. This original lacks a ruler: do not infer measured ligule height or minute bulbous hair insertion.
field_id_short_tiles.photo_status: TRUE source-verified MUCRONATA membranous ragged ligule and long SHEATH hairs photographed; original lacks 1-mm scale and individual papilla-base view

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · COUNT THE FLORETS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Tiny multi-flowered spikelets; verify glume tips and pedicel
field_id_short_tiles.details: A mature 2–4 mm Dinebra panicea complex spikelet often contains 2–4 florets. Under 20× follow the upper glume to its tiny mucro (short firm point), count REAL florets within one spikelet, and compare glumes against fertile florets. Subspecies separation requires mature glumes/fruit on correctly vouchered specimen; don't promote species-complex photo to exact mucronata. Real Jim Conrad subspecies-determined Yucatan source photo is now archived with a TRUE ruler next to attached spikelets. Use photo panel 2 to see actual size, but do not identify an individual glume-tip mucro from that image.
field_id_short_tiles.photo_status: NEW EXACT MUCRONATA GENUINE SPIKELETS + MM RULER now photographed; glume tiny mucro remains too small to resolve.
